PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert block.
RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root-cause analysis easier and avoid masking failures.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant requires exactly one Act operation or one clear scenario; non-compliant if multiple distinct Act operations or multiple scenarios are tested.
DECISION RULES: The test calls fila0.enfileira(element), fila0.imprime(), then desenfileira() twice (one expected success, one expected exception). This constitutes multiple Act operations and two distinct scenarios (successful dequeue and dequeue-from-empty) in one method. According to the rules, mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on order or shared mutable state.
RATIONALE: Independence enables parallel execution and deterministic outcomes.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use only local variables or have proper @Before/@After setup.
DECISION RULES: This test uses only local variables (Fila fila0) and does not reference or modify shared static or instance state within the method. No method-name ordering hints are present.
VERDICT: compliant

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification:
PRINCIPLE: Provide both happy-path and error-case tests for methods under test.
RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and validates exception handling.
EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant typically requires at least two test methods per behavior (one for success, one for error) or explicit exception-testing constructs.
DECISION RULES: Although this single test exercises both a successful dequeue and an exception on empty, the evaluation rules expect separate test methods for coverage (or multiple test methods across the class). The class contains only one test method overall. Per decision rules, a class with fewer than two test methods typically indicates insufficient separation; thus mark non-compliant.
VERDICT: non-compliant
